plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes of violet-blue flowers. In the sunny hills of Provence, whole fields turn purple and hum with bees, and the warm, herbal scent drifts on the summer breeze.
plants.bloomingSeason: June to August, usually at its peak in July
plants.location: Provence, southern France, and Mediterranean-climate gardens across Europe
plants.funFact: Lavender belongs to the mint family. Its flowers are rich in aromatic oils, which people have used for centuries in perfumes, soaps and calming sachets.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Daisy-like blooms with drooping rose-pink petals surround a spiky, copper-orange central cone. In prairies, meadows and sunny borders, they draw swarms of butterflies and goldfinches all summer.
plants.location: Prairies and woodland edges of the central and eastern United States, such as Minnesota and the Midwest
plants.funFact: The name Echinacea comes from the Greek word for hedgehog, a nod to the prickly central cone. In autumn, seed-eating birds feed on the seed heads.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest flower head in the protea family looks like a crown of silky pink petal-like bracts around a creamy, downy center. It blooms in the cool, bright South African winter, when little else is in flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Roughly April to October, so it is flowering in the southern hemisphere's midwinter
plants.location: Fynbos shrublands of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower. It has evolved to survive wildfires, resprouting from underground woody stems after the fynbos burns.
